tool_analysis:
Step Analysis:
- The recorded session logs into Magento admin at /admin/sales_order/, reaches the Sales > Orders grid, and exercises mass action controls.
- It demonstrates: navigating to the Orders grid, filling username and password on the login form, clicking Login, selecting per-row checkboxes, using Select Visible and Unselect Visible links, choosing an action (Hold) from the Actions dropdown, clicking Submit, and using a Status filter + Search and Order # sort header.
- Previous failures in v2 were due to a brittle selector for the login username input (input[name="login[username]"][type="text"]). In this run, the login form was interacted with using element indexes/element_hashes and visual labels, showing that the page structure is simpler than expected but still stable.

Task Definition:
- Build a reusable, deterministic tool that:
  1) Navigates directly to the Magento Sales > Orders grid URL.
  2) Handles the admin login page using robust selectors tied to element_hash (not the previously failing CSS selector).
  3) On the Orders grid, selects all visible orders via the mass action bar, applies a chosen bulk action (e.g., Cancel, Hold, Unhold, Print Invoices, etc.), and submits it.
- Filters and sorting were explored in the recording, but per the main goal (mass actions) they are not essential, so they will not be automated in the final tool to avoid unnecessary complexity.

Action Plan (essential steps only):
1) Navigation: Go to http://dockerized-magento.local/index.php/admin/sales_order/.
2) Login (if login form is shown):
   - Input username "admin" into the username field (element_hash 3597a5c5e6).
   - Input password "password123" into the password field (element_hash 1c47a5217e).
   - Click the Login button (element_hash 6831836d17).
   - Wait briefly for navigation to complete.
3) Ensure we are on the Orders grid (Orders / Sales / Magento Admin). (We will assume successful nav if the URL remains /admin/sales_order/ after login; no additional detection step is required in this tool.)
4) Select visible orders:
   - Click the Select Visible link in the mass action toolbar (element_hash 0eefac88df).
5) Choose mass action:
   - Use the Actions dropdown (element_hash e47b96fe25) and select the option specified by tool input (e.g., Hold, Cancel, Unhold, Print Invoices, etc.).
6) Submit the mass action:
   - Click the Submit button in the mass action toolbar (element_hash 4d32688149 / cc21dc812c / e5da8d6705; all refer to the same visual button in different captures; we will bind to the latest one, 4d32688149, which appeared after repeated interactions during final confirmation).
7) Optionally, wait a couple seconds for server processing (essential for predictability) and extract the admin messages area to capture any success/error feedback, but since the core task is action execution, we can keep this to a simple wait without extraction.

Variable Identification:
- The main variable is the selected bulk action from the Actions dropdown.
  - In recording, visible options were: Cancel, Hold, Unhold, Print Invoices, Print Packingslips, Print Credit Memos, Print All, Print Shipping Labels.
  - This should be an input parameter mapping to the visible text (since select_change uses visible text).
- No need to parameterize username/password for this tool, since credentials are fixed by the task specification and should not vary.
- We are not parameterizing filters, sorting, or pagination, because they are outside the minimal mass action task.

So input parameters:
- mass_action_text (string, required): visible text of the action to select in the Actions dropdown (e.g., "Hold", "Cancel").

Step Optimization:
- We avoid URL parameter manipulation because mass actions involve POSTed form state, not simple GET query changes.
- Navigation is a single direct URL step; no dashboard clicks are necessary.
- Login uses deterministic element_hash-based selectors instead of the previously failing CSS name selector.
- Orders grid interactions are limited to the essential mass action sequence: Select Visible -> choose action -> Submit.
- We add a fixed short wait between login submit and grid interaction, and another after Submit, to mitigate timing issues.
- Filters and sorting are deliberately omitted as non-essential per the core goal.

Why no additional inputs:
- The tool is intended for "perform mass actions on selected orders" by always selecting visible orders; while the UI supports more nuanced filtering and manual checkbox selection, the recorded core flow and the task description only require bulk actions on visible/all orders. For clarity and reliability, this tool focuses on that single scenario controlled solely by the choice of mass action.
name: tool_mass_action_orders.v3
description: Perform Magento admin Sales > Orders grid mass actions by selecting visible orders and applying a chosen bulk action, starting from the sales_order URL and handling the login page robustly.

steps.description: Navigate directly to the Magento Admin Sales > Orders grid URL, which may initially show the admin login page if not authenticated.
Wait briefly for the login page or orders grid to finish loading after navigation.
Enter the admin username into the username field on the login form, using a robust element_hash-based selector.
Enter the admin password into the password field on the login form, using a robust element_hash-based selector.
Click the Login button to submit the admin login form and proceed to the Orders grid.
Wait for the login request to complete and for the Orders grid page to render fully.
Click the 'Select Visible' control in the mass action toolbar to select all visible orders in the grid.
Choose the desired mass action from the 'Actions' dropdown using the provided visible text (e.g., 'Hold', 'Cancel', etc.).
Click the 'Submit' button in the mass action toolbar to apply the selected action to all selected (visible) orders.
Wait for the bulk action to be processed and any success or error message to appear above the grid.

input_schema.name: mass_action_text
input_schema.description: Visible text of the mass action to apply from the Actions dropdown, e.g., 'Hold', 'Cancel', 'Unhold', 'Print Invoices', 'Print Packingslips', 'Print Credit Memos', 'Print All', or 'Print Shipping Labels'.
